header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 min
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (InfraLabs CTO), Sofia Ramirez (Head of ML), Ethan Park (Eng Manager)
summary: InfraLabs is evaluating migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated for cost predictability and data controls. Primary concerns are API compatibility (OpenAI mapping), eval parity for model outputs, integration with vLLM/TGI stacks, and enterprise security (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Next steps: pricing, architecture docs, and a benchmark/POC scope.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus Lee, CTO at InfraLabs, good to meet you.
[00:12] Sofia: hi, Sofia, head of ML, i own model infra and evals.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan here, eng manager, i'll be the infra contact.
[00:20] Priya: Priya Patel, solutions engineer — i'll cover architecture and benchmarks.
[00:28] Alex: Awesome. quick agenda: 1) your current stack and pain points, 2) compatibility questions moving off OpenAI, 3) security and deployment options (dedicated vs private), 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Marcus: yep, perfect. we're currently on OpenAI for prod gen and embeddings, roughly 1.2B tokens/month, latency sensitive for some UX flows. cost is spiking and we need more predictable unit economics. also need stronger data controls for a couple of enterprise customers.
[00:58] Sofia: we run a bunch of evals against the same prompt sets and want parity — when we tried other hosts outputs drifted and that broke our metrics. we also use vLLM in house for fast local inference when we can.
[01:10] Priya: got it. can you say more about vLLM usage — is it in prod or for experimentation? and are you using TGI?
[01:16] Sofia: vLLM is used in some staging clusters, not full prod. we have a small TGI wrapper for a couple of models for latency testing. main prod path is OpenAI endpts.
[01:26] Alex: thanks. so primary drivers are cost predictability and data residency / controls — sounds like Redwood Dedicated or Private would be the fit. quick Q on compatibility: how important is OpenAI API parity vs feature parity (function calling, streaming, embeddings)?
[01:38] Marcus: OpenAI API parity is important — we have SDKs built on that surface area. function calling and streaming are used in a few flows. embeddings are used for search and reranking.
[01:48] Priya: Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints for many models — we also map function calling and streaming. there are edge cases with custom tool calls and some structured output parsing, we can walk through those. side note: sometimes transcriptors show model names slightly different — we call out the mapping in docs.
[02:00] Ethan: how about model eval parity? we need output stability — can't have hallucination spikes. when you say "mapping" does that change logits or sampling defaults?
[02:08] Priya: great question. mapping is API mapping not model weights. we onboard model variants and have verified performance profiles. for production we recommend running your eval sets on the target model build inside Redwood. that's part of a POC. some minor differences can occur because of tokenizers or quantization; we capture those in our eval report.
[02:28] Marcus: tokenization differences — that was one of our previous surprises when we tried another host, prompts tokenized differently and cut off.
[02:34] Priya: yep, we log token counts and provide tokenizer mappings. for sponsored models we supply the same BPE behavior; if you're running a community model with quantization, we surface the differences.
[02:44] Alex: on cost, we typically show dedicated reserved capacity with per-token economics that drop as you commit. we also surface batching and KV cache benefits — depending on your seq lengths and reuse, savings can be material.
[02:58] Sofia: can Redwood run with our existing vLLM/TGI wrappers? we prefer to keep some of our local tooling.
[03:06] Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports running customer-managed runtimes in private deployment patterns. for dedicated we run our runtime optimized kernels; but you can keep local vLLM for dev. for POC we can run comparative benchmarks: your TGI/vLLM config vs our dedicated runtime using the same model checkpoints.
[03:22] Ethan: latency — what's typical p95 for generation on dedicated infra versus OpenAI?
[03:28] Priya: depends on model size and instance type. for a 13B-like family on our dedicated pool we often see p95 similar or slightly better than hosted depending on network egress; typical numbers i've seen are 80-120ms per token for mid-sized models with continuous batching turned on, but we'll run your workload to get exacts.
[03:45] Marcus: network egress concerns us — some of our customers require data to stay in region. can you do region pinning?
[03:52] Alex: yes, Dedicated supports region pinning and Private supports customer VPC or on-prem where no traffic leaves the network. also KMS/HSM integrations available.
[04:00] Sofia: SOC2 and audit logs — we need to show our customers the logs and retention policies.
[04:05] Alex: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, and audit logs. Priya can share the security pack after the call.
[04:12] Priya: i'll drop the security deck and KMS integration notes. also we have a compliance pack that details retention and deletion flows.
[04:18] Marcus: great. another question: we sometimes run streaming calls and need to support partial responses and reconnects gracefully. does Redwood handle that?
[04:26] Priya: yes — streaming API with reconnect semantics and chunked responses. there are a few edge cases with websocket timeouts behind proxies but we have guidance.
[04:34] Ethan: about the migration effort — how long does a typical discovery->POC->prod take?
[04:40] Alex: from discovery to pilot usually 3-6 weeks depending on availability and scope; full prod rollout with data residency and contract can be 8-12 weeks typically.
[04:48] Sofia: for us the gating items are: eval parity, throughput tests at our peak, and FIPS/KMS for some customers.
[04:55] Priya: understood. for the POC scope we recommend: 1) run your eval set against the target model in Redwood Dedicated, 2) run throughput and p95 latency tests with your token profile, 3) validate integrations (embeddings indexing, function calls), 4) security review.
[05:12] Marcus: sounds good. about deployments: does Dedicated mean Redwood manages the infra or you provision a dedicated pool inside Redwood cloud?
[05:20] Priya: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's cloud dedicated to your org — we manage orchestration but capacity is isolated; Private is when you want the control in your VPC or on-prem. both can integrate with your KMS and audit requirements.
[05:33] Ethan: for Dedicated, what level of control do we get for things like kernel/quantization choices?
[05:39] Priya: we expose quantization profiles and there are tuning knobs; for very custom builds we can coordinate a private deployment. generally customers use our recommended profiles and we manage validation.
[05:48] Marcus: benchmarking — we'll need a simple script to reproduce. can you provide one?
[05:53] Priya: yes, we'll share a benchmarking harness and guidance to run it against your token profile. we'll also accept your workload as a dataset and run it on our side if you prefer.
[06:03] Sofia: what about model versions — we have pinned model variants in prod. how are rollouts handled?
[06:09] Alex: Redwood supports version pinning and can do canary rollouts, A/B routing by route, and auto-fallback policies. you'll be able to pin per-route via the console and set traffic split.
[06:20] Ethan: do you integrate with Datadog / our observability stack?
[06:24] Priya: yes — we have hooks and tracing for datadog and open telemetry; you can get token-level cost breakdowns and route dashboards.
[06:31] Marcus: any known gotchas when replacing OpenAI with a dedicated open model? especially for embeddings?
[06:37] Priya: embeddings vary by model family — for semantic search you might see slightly different vector geometry. we recommend reindexing and running your similarity thresholds during the POC. we also provide evaluation tooling that calculates recall/precision differences.
[06:50] Sofia: how do you handle prompts that used OpenAI system messages heavily? some of those relied on specific system behavior.
[06:57] Priya: system message semantics are preserved in our mapping, but behavior can differ slightly by model. part of the eval is checking for drift and adjusting prompts; we can help recommend guardrails and prompt templates.
[07:10] Marcus: ok, regarding costs — can you share an example TCO comparison vs OpenAI?
[07:15] Alex: yes — we'll send a TCO spreadsheet. typically customers at your scale (1M+ tokens/month) see meaningful savings on Dedicated with reserved commits, especially when combined with KV caching and batching. exact delta depends on call patterns.
[07:28] Ethan: one technical ask: we're using a custom tokenizer plugin in vLLM. will that break things?
[07:35] Priya: custom tokenizers can be supported in Private deployments; in Dedicated it depends — if it's a bespoke tokenizer that changes tokenization semantics, we need to coordinate. for the POC bring a few examples and we'll test.
[07:46] Marcus: what's your SLA for Dedicated?
[07:49] Alex: Dedicated has an SLA with uptime targets and latency SLOs depending on contract tier. premium SLA available for enterprise deals.
[07:57] Sofia: okay, last architecture question: can we route by cost vs latency automatically? e.g. cheaper model for low-risk flows and higher quality for critical flows?
[08:06] Priya: yes — smart routing policies let you route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. you can set automatic fallback when capacity is constrained.
[08:15] Marcus: perfect. any red flags you see from what i described?
[08:19] Priya: nothing major — we just need the eval set and workload profiles so we can quantify drift and performance. we'll also validate your tokenization and embedding geometry.
[08:29] Alex: to recap next steps, we'll send pricing + TCO, Priya will share architecture/compatibility notes and the benchmark harness, and you (InfraLabs) will share eval sets and coordinate infra access for benchmarking.
[08:43] Marcus: agreed. timeline — can we aim to kick off the POC next week?
[08:47] Alex: yes, if we have eval data and access early next week we can align resources.
[08:52] Ethan: i will provision guest access and coordinate with priya.
[08:56] Sofia: i'll start exporting the evals and prompts, probably by Monday.
[09:00] Priya: i'll put together the POC scope doc and check the available slots for next week.
[09:06] Alex: great. final quick Q from me — any procurement constraints or legal red flags we should know about?
[09:11] Marcus: we'll need standard data processing addendum, plus a clause for regional data residency. procurement will review once we have pricing.
[09:18] Alex: understood. we'll include DPA language in the pricing email.
[09:22] Marcus: thanks everyone, excited to see the benchmarks.
[09:25] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with the decks and pricing.
[09:30] [call ends — 43:12]
